title: Disciplinary logging and AAP reporting practice - historical archive evidence
summary: Historical disciplinary activity was maintained in annual restricted workbooks and repeatedly transformed into AAP-sorted reporting copies. The corpus now documents register coverage, schema evolution, inconsistent warning labels, AAP transformation behavior and post-2023 coverage gaps without preserving employee-level records.

claims.claim: The supplied archive contains 17 distinct restricted disciplinary-action workbooks labeled by fiscal year, covering 2008-2009 through 2023-2024 plus 2025-2026; no 2024-2025 fiscal-year workbook was present in this upload.

evidence.note: Employee-level workbook contents were not committed or generalized.

claims.claim: The archive contains 11 distinct restricted disciplinary-log workbooks explicitly organized as AAP-sorted copies for periods from 2013-2014 through 2022-2023, including two distinct 2016-2017 artifacts.

evidence.note: This establishes archive structure, not the employee-level contents of the workbooks.

claims.claim: The repeated AAP-sorted copies suggest that disciplinary log data was historically reorganized or prepared for AAP-related reporting.

evidence.note: Inference from repeated source naming/organization; exact AAP use should be validated against plan instructions.

claims.claim: A separate restricted verbal-warning workbook exists in the archive, indicating verbal warnings may have been tracked separately from the fiscal-year disciplinary-action logs.

The supplied annual disciplinary registers provide near-continuous fiscal-year evidence from 2009-2010 through 2022-2023, plus a 2008-2009 file containing records beginning April 2008; the 2023-2024 file is only populated through September 22, 2023, no 2024-2025 fiscal-year workbook is present, and the supplied 2025-2026 workbook is an empty template.

evidence.note: A missing/empty workbook is a source-coverage gap, not evidence that no discipline occurred.

claims.claim: The annual register schema evolved from department/name/job/gender/origin/type/date/reason/EEO-1 in 2008-2009, to an EEO-1/gender/race schema from 2009-2014, then added Veteran and IWD fields beginning in 2014-2015.

Historical discipline-type values are not normalized: examples include WW1/WWI, WW2/WWII, WW3/WWIII, WW4/WWIV, Verbal/verbal, Counsel/Counseling, Warning, Final, Incident and Infraction. The labels must not be mechanically mapped to current disciplinary groups.

Free-text historical reasons cluster broadly around work/performance, attendance, policy violations, vehicle incidents, safety, tardiness/leaving early, customer/coworker conduct, cash/deposits/fares and smaller operational categories; these categories are derived multi-label analysis rather than an official RTEC taxonomy.

evidence.note: Categories overlap and are not suitable as official disciplinary codes without validation.

claims.claim: AAP-sorted disciplinary copies changed layout year to year, sometimes preserving type/reason/date and sometimes reducing to reporting/demographic fields; several include hard-coded subgroup subtotal rows and no formulas were detected.

Two materially different 2016-2017 AAP-sorted derivatives exist: one retains event date with no type/reason and no detected subtotal rows, while another strips the date and contains hard-coded subgroup count rows.

evidence.note: The later/refined status of either version is not assumed without authority metadata.

trigger: Disciplinary action or verbal warning is documented; AAP reporting may require a historical disciplinary-data extract.
prerequisites: Validated current discipline-recording policy and privacy/access controls.
steps: Record each disciplinary/incident event in the authoritative restricted register.
Maintain fiscal-year coverage and schema/version metadata.
Normalize historical labels only in a derived analytical layer; preserve source values for provenance.
Generate AAP-specific reporting views from authoritative records rather than manually copying/re-sorting workbooks.
Detect and separate detail rows from subtotal/count rows.
decisions: Which current disciplinary events belong in the reporting population.
Which fields may be used in AAP analysis under current policy and privacy rules.
deadlines: Historical files were organized by fiscal year; exact reporting deadlines are not established by this evidence.
controls: Do not duplicate authoritative case records merely to create reporting views when a controlled derived report can be generated.
Keep employee-level disciplinary and protected-characteristic data restricted.
Never treat a missing fiscal-year file or an empty template as proof of zero disciplinary events.
Preserve raw historical type/reason values while maintaining normalized derived categories separately.
AAP parsers must be schema-aware and must identify subtotal/count rows before treating a row as an employee/event record.
Current discipline decisions must use the current handbook/process, not historical WW labels.
unresolved_questions: Was disciplinary activity after September 22, 2023 moved to another system/file, and where is the authoritative 2024-2025/current register?
What exactly did historical WW1-WW9/WWI-WWIV labels mean in each era, and were they local warning sequence labels or policy-defined levels?
Why are there two distinct 2016-2017 AAP-sorted derivatives, and which was used for the final AAP analysis?
What current AAP discipline-analysis requirement, if any, supersedes the manual sorted-workbook practice?
automation_candidates: Maintain one authoritative restricted disciplinary-event register and generate fiscal-year/AAP views on demand.
Normalize historical warning-stage labels with an explicit source-to-normalized mapping and confidence rather than string replacement.
Schema-detect annual/AAP workbook variants and classify each row as detail/header/subtotal before import.
Automatically flag partial/missing fiscal-year coverage and empty-template years before AAP/audit reporting.
Generate privacy-safe aggregate AAP analyses without duplicating employee-level rosters.

provenance.notes: Derived only from privacy-safe file classes, periods, and hashes; no employee case content was used.
No employee identifiers or protected-class counts stored.
